title.es: Dar una charla de cinco minutos

es: Preparar y ajustar una charla breve sobre una pasión personal: apertura con gancho, tres ideas con señales, cierre con takeaway y respuesta a una pregunta del público.

vocabulary.es: idea final que se llevan los oyentes

teaching.en: Speaking about a passion lets you speak from the heart, but even a beginner should rehearse out loud before the day.
teaching.es: Hablar de una pasión te permite hablar con el corazón, pero incluso un principiante debe ensayar en voz alta antes del día.
teaching.explanationEs: Speak from the heart es hablar con sinceridad; rehearse out loud es ensayar con la voz, no solo releer.
segments: Speaking about a passion lets you speak from the heart, but
even a beginner should rehearse out loud before the day.
teaching.audioText: Speaking about a passion lets you speak from the heart, but even a beginner should rehearse out loud before the day.

teaching.en: A show of hands at the start tells you whether most of the room has ever seen a harvest.
teaching.es: Una votación a mano alzada al comienzo te dice si la mayoría de la sala ha visto alguna vez una cosecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Un gesto del público sirve como gancho y como información: adapta el nivel de tu charla a quien escucha.
segments: A show of hands at the start tells you whether
most of the room has ever seen a harvest.
teaching.audioText: A show of hands at the start tells you whether most of the room has ever seen a harvest.

teaching.en: When her timing slipped, she decided to pick up the pace and cut the third example.
teaching.es: Cuando su ritmo se desajustó, decidió acelerar y eliminar el tercer ejemplo.
teaching.explanationEs: Pick up the pace es acelerar; en una charla de cinco minutos, cortar es mejor que correr sin pausa.
segments: When her timing slipped, she decided to pick
up the pace and cut the third example.
teaching.audioText: When her timing slipped, she decided to pick up the pace and cut the third example.

teaching.en: Nobody remembers every idea, so stay on message and end with one takeaway that listeners can repeat to a friend.
teaching.es: Nadie recuerda todas las ideas, así que no te salgas del mensaje y termina con una idea que los oyentes puedan repetir a un amigo.
teaching.explanationEs: Stay on message: cada ejemplo debe servir al mismo mensaje; el takeaway es su versión más corta.
segments: Nobody remembers every idea, so stay on message and end
with one takeaway that listeners can repeat to a friend.
teaching.audioText: Nobody remembers every idea, so stay on message and end with one takeaway that listeners can repeat to a friend.

teaching.en: If you can field a question calmly and with passion, you leave a lasting impression long after the room empties.
teaching.es: Si sabes responder una pregunta con calma y con pasión, dejas una impresión duradera mucho después de que la sala se vacíe.
teaching.explanationEs: Field a question es manejar una pregunta imprevista; la calma importa tanto como el contenido.

prompt.es: Elige el gancho más eficaz para abrir una charla sobre correr.

choices.text: Good morning. Today I will speak about running, which many people enjoy.
Have you ever run so slowly that a walker passed you?
Running is a sport that has existed for thousands of years.

feedback.es: Una pregunta personal y un poco humillante despierta curiosidad; las otras dos anuncian el tema o dan un dato general sin crear interés.

hint.es: El gancho no anuncia el tema: despierta curiosidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando su charla empezó a alargarse, tuvo que acelerar el ritmo.»

feedback.es: Pick up the pace es la expresión fija para acelerar; en una charla corta, recortar es mejor que correr.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que significa «ritmo» en pick up the ___.

origin.text: The organisers gave each speaker five minutes. When her talk began to run long, she had to pick up the ___ and cut her last example.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mantén el mensaje y termina con una idea clara que llevarse.»

answer.text: Stay on message and end with one clear takeaway

feedback.es: Stay on message mantiene cada ejemplo al servicio de la idea principal, y one clear takeaway es el cierre.

hint.es: Empieza con la expresión que significa «no salirse del mensaje».

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿cómo responde la oradora a la pregunta sobre el costo?

choices.text: She reassures beginners but urges them to buy proper equipment first.
She avoids giving a price and promises to answer it after the talk.
She reassures beginners that they can start with almost nothing.

feedback.es: Agradece la pregunta, responde con lo que hace falta para empezar y comprueba si ha quedado claro.

origin.audio: Good question, and thank you. Football is not expensive: all you need is a ball and a friend. I started with one old ball and a small field behind my house. So please do not wait for perfect shoes. Does that answer it?

prompt.es: ¿Qué tipo de apertura usa el orador en este texto?

choices.text: An anecdote that builds suspense through a small setback.
A promise that reassures beginners from the very first line.
A rhetorical question that invites listeners to imagine.

feedback.es: Cuenta un episodio personal (la semilla que tarda en brotar) y mantiene la intriga con un pequeño contratiempo: una anécdota.

origin.text: Last spring, I planted a single seed. For two weeks, nothing happened, and I almost gave up. Then, one morning, something tiny and green pushed through the soil, and I felt as proud as if I had built a house.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la charla.

pairs: Have you ever grown your own food?
First, start small; moreover, be patient.
Seldom have I felt so proud of a plant.
Good question. Let me field it briefly.
A show of hands, please, if you have ever tasted a real harvest.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: abrir, ordenar ideas, dar énfasis, atender una pregunta o hacer participar a la sala.

prompt.es: Escribe tu charla de cinco minutos: gancho, tres ideas, cierre y respuesta.

answer.text: Quick question: how many of you have ever lost a tennis match to a ten-year-old? I have, and it changed my life. Three years ago, I was a beginner at our neighbourhood tennis club, and I wanted to quit after one week. Today I will tell you why I stayed. First, tennis taught me patience: I learned to wait before I move. Moreover, the club gave me friends who explained every mistake without laughing. Having said that, nobody ever made me feel small. Second, tennis changed how I deal with problems at work. Seldom have I felt so calm under pressure. Third, it costs almost nothing. You only need a ball and a friend. To sum up, be patient, be curious and never stop trying. That is my takeaway. And remember the ten-year-old? Last week, I beat her. Thank you for your question: you asked whether you must be good to join. Not at all; beginners are the heart of our club.
accepted: Quick question: how many of you have ever lost a tennis match to a ten-year-old? I have, and it changed my life. Three years ago, I was a beginner at our neighbourhood tennis club, and I wanted to quit after one week. Today I will tell you why I stayed. First, tennis taught me patience: I learned to wait before I move. Moreover, the club gave me friends who explained every mistake without laughing. Having said that, nobody ever made me feel small. Second, tennis changed how I deal with problems at work. Seldom have I felt so calm under pressure. Third, it costs almost nothing. You only need a ball and a friend. To sum up, be patient, be curious and never stop trying. That is my takeaway. And remember the ten-year-old? Last week, I beat her. Thank you for your question: you asked whether you must be good to join. Not at all; beginners are the heart of our club.

Did you know that nine out of ten people who start a book club give up before the third meeting? I almost did. Last year I was a beginner, too shy to speak, and I told myself that nobody wanted my opinion. Today I will show you how I changed my mind. First, I chose a book that I loved, because passion is easier to share than duty. Moreover, I wrote down one question before every meeting. Second, I listened, and having said that, I also learned to disagree politely. Not only did the club improve my reading, but it also gave me the courage to speak in front of strangers. Third, I kept going even when the book was difficult. In conclusion, choose well, prepare one question and stay for the whole evening. That is my message. Good question, by the way: you asked whether you must be a fast reader to join. Not at all; slow readers often say the most interesting things.

feedback.es: Una charla completa abre con gancho, ordena tres ideas con señales, cierra con un takeaway y atiende la pregunta del público.

origin.text: Tema: un club o afición de tu barrio (tenis, lectura, remo…). Escribe en inglés una charla (170–250 palabras): un gancho (pregunta o anécdota), tres ideas con señales (First, Moreover, Second…), una inversión o una regla de tres, un cierre con takeaway y una respuesta a un oyente que pregunta si hace falta ser bueno para unirse.

evidenceGroups: i would like you to remember

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué recurso usa la oradora para abrir su charla?

choices.text: A story about a famous rower whom she admired.
A statistic that she applies at once to herself.
A promise to teach the audience how to row.

feedback.es: Abre con una cifra («nine out of ten») y la aplica enseguida a su propia experiencia.

origin.audio: Nine out of ten beginners quit a new sport in the first month, and I was nearly one of them. Three winters ago, I joined a rowing club at six in the morning, and for two weeks I hated every minute. First, I kept going because nobody laughed at my mistakes. Moreover, the club asked only that I turn up. Having said that, nothing was easy, and I never pretended otherwise. Seldom have I been so tired, and rarely have I been so proud. So if you are starting something new, find people who will wait for you.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender sobre la actitud del club hacia los principiantes?

choices.text: That it kept newcomers apart from its more experienced members.
That it expected every beginner to improve within a month.
That it valued commitment more than natural skill.

feedback.es: Nadie se reía de los errores y solo se pedía que se presentara: se valoraba la constancia por encima de la habilidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nadie esperaba una pregunta tan directa, pero ella supo responderla con calma.»

feedback.es: Field a question es manejar con soltura una pregunta imprevista; handle o answer son alternativas defendibles.

origin.text: Nobody in the audience expected such a blunt question, but the speaker managed to ___ it calmly and then returned to her main point.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el propósito principal de este consejo del entrenador?

choices.text: To persuade speakers to fix their structure but keep the wording flexible.
To warn speakers that a rehearsed talk is always a bad one.
To recommend that speakers write every word they plan to say.

feedback.es: Pide ensayar sin aprender cada palabra de memoria: conocer la estructura y dejar respirar el resto.

origin.text: Rehearse out loud, but do not learn every word by heart. A talk that is learned by heart sounds like a recording, and the first unexpected question will push it off course. Know your three ideas, know your first line, and let the rest breathe.

prompt.es: Ordena: «No fue hasta el cierre cuando reveló su idea final.»

answer.text: Not until the closing did she reveal her takeaway

feedback.es: Not until + expresión de tiempo invierte el orden: did va antes de she y reveal queda en base.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender la oradora sobre los nervios?

choices.text: That they disappear completely once she has enough practice.
That they are normal and can be managed with preparation.
That they reveal how little she has prepared for each talk.

feedback.es: Admite que siempre los siente, pero describe cómo los maneja: ensayo y recordar que el público está de su parte.

origin.audio: You asked whether I get nervous before a talk. Honestly, every single time. But I rehearse out loud, I pick up the pace when I feel my voice shake, and I remember that nobody in the room wants me to do badly.
